scenes.headline: How an embedded database finds the nearest vectors
scenes.sub: zvec: a graph walk, cheap int8 codes, and an exact re-rank, all in-process.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Peony! zvec is Alibaba's open-source vector database that links into your app, like SQLite. Here's how it searches ten million vectors fast.

scenes.text: Vector search as a library, like SQLite: no server, no network hop. Inside, a graph walk visits few vectors, and cheap codes make each score fast.
scenes.say: The idea: vector search as a library, like SQLite. No server, no network hop. Two standard levers make it fast: visit fewer vectors, and make each score cheap.

left.title: Brute force
items: Score the query against every vector
left.say: Brute force scores the query against all ten million vectors. Correct, and far too slow.

right.title: HNSW graph walk
items: Wire each vector to its nearest neighbours
Hop to whichever neighbour is closer
right.say: HNSW wires each vector to its neighbours, then walks: hop to whichever is closer, stop at a local minimum. Visits grow roughly logarithmically.

scenes.title: Lever two: cheap scores, then exact ones

steps.say: A query walks the HNSW graph, fifty links per node. Every hop is scored with int8 codes: seven hundred sixty-eight bytes a vector, not three thousand seventy-two.

steps.note: a wider ef frontier: more recall, fewer QPS
steps.say: The walk keeps a frontier a hundred and eighteen wide, and returns a shortlist. But cheap codes distort distances, so its order is wrong.
So the refiner re-scores just the shortlist with the original full-precision vectors.
The int8 pass only filters. Full-precision math decides the final order.

scenes.title: VectorDBBench, Cohere 10M
scenes.note: Self-reported. zvec's number has no network in it; hardware differs per row.
scenes.say: zvec reports eight thousand four hundred seventy-five queries a second, roughly twice the next entry. It's self-reported, with no network in it, beside managed services on different hardware.

scenes.text: Visit fewer vectors, make each score cheap, then re-rank exactly: standard levers, packaged to live inside your app.

recap: HNSW visits a logarithmic slice of the data
int8 codes filter; full precision decides the order
One writer, many readers, like SQLite
scenes.say: To recap: a graph walk, cheap codes that only filter, and an exact re-rank, all inside your app.
